name: Ori and the Will of the Wisps

Optimal.Notes: At native 1280x800 with high textures and medium shadows, the Deck handles this game effortlessly at a locked 60 fps — the sweet spot of great visuals, smooth gameplay, and reasonable battery life. Motion blur is disabled as it can feel excessive in a fast-moving platformer.

profiles.Summary: Ori and the Will of the Wisps is a visually stunning 2D action-platformer that runs very well on the Steam Deck, comfortably exceeding its PC recommended specs and achieving smooth, high-framerate play. The game is Deck Verified (Playable) with a strong gold/trending platinum ProtonDB rating, indicating a largely trouble-free experience out of the box.
profiles.BasisNote: No Deck-specific player reports were found; profiles are estimated from the PC minimum/recommended specs and the Deck's hardware — this 2D platformer's requirements are well below the Deck's capability, so high framerates are expected. On your first run, check the frame counter in a busy combat area with lots of particle effects to confirm the 60 fps or 90 fps target holds.

MaxBattery.Notes: Rendering at 960x600 with FSR upscaling to 1280x800 and a 6 W TDP cap dramatically extends battery life while keeping the game very playable. This 2D-heavy game looks great even at reduced resolution thanks to its art style.

KnownIssues: No Deck-specific player reports were found; issues are estimated from general ProtonDB gold/platinum data.
Some PC players report occasional stutters during large particle effects or busy combat sequences.
HDR support is available and may require manual configuration in-game on Linux/Proton.
The game targets Windows 10 and runs via Proton; rare launch issues have been reported on gold-tier titles.

MaxPerformance.Notes: With TDP uncapped and the OLED's 90 Hz refresh rate, this lightweight 2D game can push close to 90 fps at max settings — a genuinely silky experience. Battery life will be short, so best suited for plugged-in or short sessions.
